Definition: from G573; singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal):--bountifulness, liberal(-ity), simplicity, singleness.
BiblicalUsage: Haplotes is singleness of heart, a life without a second face, and Paul ties it to giving. In 2 Corinthians 8:2 the churches of Macedonia gave out of deep poverty with the riches of their liberality, in 2 Corinthians 9:11 that liberality works thanksgiving to God, in Romans 12:8 the giver is to give with simplicity, and in Colossians 3:22 servants are to obey with singleness of heart.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe singleness is the opposite of the divided life: one heart, one motive, no performance. The Macedonians gave from poverty because their hearts were not split, and that is the giving God loves.
